articles.title: DEEP SKY OBSERVING
articles.summary: This article presents a deep-sky observing list compiled by Mark Wagner for March 2008, covering the period from the third quarter to new moon. It details a selection of galaxies and open clusters, ordered from north to south, providing astronomical data, challenge ratings (1-4), and descriptive observing notes for each target. The full list is available online, with this excerpt focusing on objects within one hour of right ascension.

articles.title: Zosma
articles.summary: The article provides an in-depth look at Zosma (Delta Leonis), an A4 star in the Leo constellation, detailing its etymology, physical characteristics like rapid rotation and luminosity, and its membership in the Ursa Major Stream. It discusses Zosma's potential as a Delta Scuti variable and its status as a triple star system, while also touching upon broader astronomical concepts like Bayer star naming conventions and the OBAFGKM stellar classification system.

articles.title: Notification of May General Meeting
articles.summary: Due to insufficient time before the February meeting, the club will hold a second General Meeting in May to vote on three proposed amendments to its bylaws. These amendments aim to improve procedures regarding the definition of board member absence, qualifications for board membership, and the notification process for director candidates. The board believes these changes are in the best interest of the club.

articles.title: Geoff Marcy on March 5, 2008 at 7 p.m.
articles.summary: Astronomer Geoff Marcy of UC Berkeley will deliver a non-technical, illustrated talk titled "New Worlds and Yellowstone: How Common are Habitable Planets?" on March 5, 2008, at 7 p.m. The lecture, part of the Silicon Valley Astronomy Lectures at Foothill College, will discuss the search for exoplanets, including Earth-like worlds and extraterrestrial intelligence, and what future telescopes might find. The event is free and open to the public.

articles.title: No Mars Rock Unturned
articles.summary: The Mars rovers Spirit and Opportunity currently face limitations in immediate data collection of interesting rocks due to communication delays with Earth. To overcome this, JPL has developed AEGIS (Autonomous Exploration for Gathering Increased Science) software. This artificial intelligence allows rovers to autonomously identify and capture high-resolution images and data of intriguing geological features without waiting for human commands, thereby preventing missed scientific opportunities.

articles.title: Letter from the President
articles.summary: The President's letter reviews a year of significant improvements for the club, including revitalized beginner programs, a new website, a new Beginner's Workshop, and major investments in the loaner telescope program. It also highlights increased board involvement, the return of CalStar to its roots, and ongoing school outreach, with plans for continued growth and member engagement. The document also includes a brief summary of recent astronomy news.

articles.title: Messier Marathon
articles.summary: The article announces the annual Messier Marathon, hosted by the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) at Henry Coe State Park on Saturday, March 8th. It details the event's purpose, which is to locate all 110 Messier objects in one night, highlighting skill development in efficient chart usage and object identification over simple viewing. Participants are strongly advised to prepare with excellent charts, detailed strategies, and checklists.
